# Site-Selection Note: South & West Regions

Houston Food & Beverage Stores and Phoenix Restaurants & Food Service represent the strongest expansion targets, combining high opportunity scores with low penetration.

| Rank | Metro | Category | Penetration | Opportunity Score | White Space |
|------|-------|----------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|
| 1 | Houston | Food & Beverage Stores | 8% [F1] | 9.52 [F1] | $5.5B [F1] |
| 2 | Phoenix | Restaurants & Food Service | 6% [F2] | 8.65 [F2] | $2.9B [F2] |
| 3 | Denver | Food & Beverage Stores | 20% [F3] | 8.29 [F3] | $1.5B [F3] |
| 4 | Dallas | Food & Beverage Stores | 20% [F4] | 8.25 [F4] | $2.8B [F4] |
| 5 | Phoenix | Food & Beverage Stores | 21% [F5] | 8.18 [F5] | $3.5B [F5] |
| 6 | Los Angeles | Food & Beverage Stores | 24% [F6] | 7.87 [F6] | $7.7B [F6] |
| 7 | Atlanta | Food & Beverage Stores | 24% [F7] | 7.85 [F7] | $1.0B [F7] |
| 8 | Miami | Food & Beverage Stores | 25% [F8] | 7.80 [F8] | $0.9B [F8] |

- Houston leads with the highest opportunity score of 9.52 [F1] and minimal 8% [F1] penetration in Food & Beverage Stores, representing $5.5B [F1] in white space across a category experiencing 10.35% [F1] demand growth.
- Phoenix presents a dual opportunity, ranking second overall in Restaurants & Food Service at 6% [F2] penetration and fifth in Food & Beverage Stores at 21% [F5] penetration, totaling $6.4B in combined white space.
- Los Angeles holds the largest white-space pool at $7.7B [F6] but ranks sixth in opportunity score at 7.87 [F6], reflecting higher 24% [F6] penetration that diminishes the growth-gap advantage relative to underpenetrated markets.

## Data Coverage
Facts F1–F8 used. No data estimates or forecasts included.
